english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning the Man who is ugly in his Body, [but] beautiful [in his Soul].
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter contains no identifiable cosmological-correspondential substrate. It is entirely later material: apostolic narrative about Mani publicly embracing a deformed elect member (¶1-7), natural-philosophical teaching about pearl formation used as parable vehicle (¶9-13), parable interpretation mapping to institutional and cosmic entities (¶14-17), and exhortation closure (¶18). While cosmic vocabulary appears in ¶16-17 (aeons of light, aeons of greatness, light-givers), it serves parable interpretation rather than constituting standalone systematic cosmological teaching. The pearl natural philosophy, while historically interesting (as Gardner notes), is Mani's own pedagogical content, not pre-Mani substrate. Teaching purity is very low (0.186). The Gospel citation in ¶6 ('the saviour says') confirms the chapter's late editorial composition.
